run.reviewer: Fresh-context agent distinct from primary auditor who authored these supplemental cases; exact provider model/version not exposed
run.notes: First-pass static review, 10 new randomized workflow cases. No expected labels or original repository supplied. Explicit trusted synthetic contracts. No target execution. Observations retained without edits.

findings.reason: Static evidence under the supplied synthetic contract: the guard establishes only that the actor role has an invitation policy; it never checks whether the requested role belongs to that policy. A manager or administrator can record an administrator invitation, and a manager can record a manager invitation, violating the explicit grant limits. The contract states recorded invitation roles are granted without another filter.
findings.source: Caller-controlled role argument to invite; verified actor.role selects allowedInvites, whose policy arrays are defined in policy.js:1.
findings.sink: app.js:4 appends the unchecked role to the server-owned invitations list for actor.tenantId.
findings.remediation: Before appending, require the requested role to occur in the actor-specific allowedInvites array, with a fail-closed result for actors without an allowed role. Preserve the tenant derived from the verified actor.

findings.reason: Static evidence under the supplied synthetic contract: the guard checks reward ownership and account existence but omits reward.used. Setting used after crediting does not prevent another call from crediting the same server-issued reward again. This violates the single-redemption invariant even in the complete synchronous single-process model; no race premise is needed.
findings.source: Verified reward owner supplies rewardId on successive redeem calls; amount remains server-owned and immutable.
findings.sink: app.js:6 adds reward.amount to account.credit on every accepted call, including calls after reward.used was set.
findings.remediation: Reject already-used rewards before crediting and retain consumption with the credit mutation as one synchronous operation in this model. If storage later becomes asynchronous or distributed, enforce consumption and crediting atomically.

findings.reason: Static evidence under the supplied synthetic contract: the state guard rejects only shipped orders. An owner in the correct tenant can therefore ship an order in an unpaid state, bypassing the required settled-payment transition. The ownership and tenant checks limit affected orders but do not enforce payment.
findings.source: Verified customer chooses an owned orderId whose server-owned order state is not paid and not shipped.
findings.sink: app.js:6 records a shipment before app.js:7 changes the order state to shipped; the contract gives this effect inventory and goods consequences.
findings.remediation: Require order.state to equal paid before creating a shipment, then transition it to shipped within the same synchronous operation. Reject every other prior state.

findings.reason: Static evidence under the supplied synthetic contract: the token is checked for account binding, expiry and prior use, but the requested email is never compared with token.email. A user with a valid token delivered to their bound address can mark a different caller-chosen address verified without proving control of it. This establishes false email verification; downstream account takeover is not established by the snippet.
findings.source: Authenticated user supplies requestedEmail and a valid unused email-verification token bound to their own account and token.email.
findings.sink: app.js:6 assigns requestedEmail, and app.js:7 marks that address verified.
findings.remediation: Require requestedEmail to equal the token-bound address and assign user.email from token.email before marking it verified. Preserve account binding, expiry and single-use checks.

findings.reason: Static evidence under the supplied synthetic contract: a valid unused unexpired recovery token authorizes a password update selected by requestedUserId without comparing that identifier with token.userId. A caller who possesses a legitimate token for their own account and knows another existing account identifier can replace that other account password with caller-chosen credentials. Token unpredictability, expiry and consumption do not establish target-account binding.
findings.source: Public recover caller supplies requestedUserId and a trusted-adapter digest of caller-chosen credentials, together with a valid token for a different account.
findings.sink: app.js:7 replaces the passwordDigest of the account selected by requestedUserId at app.js:4.
findings.remediation: Resolve the account from token.userId, or reject any requestedUserId that differs from token.userId, before consuming the token and updating credentials.
